entities.name: Medusa Ransomware
entities.evidence: Medusa is a ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS) variant first identified in June 2021.

entities.name: Medusa operations
entities.evidence: Medusa actors have impacted over 500 victims from a variety of critical infrastructure sectors.

entities.name: Phishing campaigns
entities.evidence: Phishing campaigns as a primary method for stealing victim credentials [T1566].

entities.name: Exploitation of unpatched software vulnerabilities
entities.evidence: Exploitation of unpatched software vulnerabilities [T1190] through Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) such as:

entities.name: CVE-2024-1709
entities.evidence: ScreenConnect vulnerability CVE-2024-1709 [CWE-288: Authentication Bypass Using an Alternate Path or Channel].

entities.name: CVE-2023-48788
entities.evidence: Fortinet EMS SQL injection vulnerability CVE-2023-48788 [CWE 89: SQL Injection].

entities.name: CVE-2025-10035
entities.evidence: Fortra GoAnywhere vulnerability CVE-2025-10035 [CWE-502: Deserialization of Untrusted Data].

entities.name: CVE-2026-1731
entities.evidence: BeyondTrust vulnerability CVE-2026-1731 [CWE-78: OS Command Injection].

entities.name: Healthcare and Public Health (HPH) Sector
entities.evidence: The Healthcare and Public Health (HPH) Sector has been a frequent victim of Medusa operations.

entities.name: Use of PowerShell
entities.evidence: Medusa actors use PowerShell [T1059.001] and the Windows Command Prompt (cmd.exe) [T1059.003] for network [T1046] and filesystem enumeration [T1083] and to utilize Ingress Tool Transfer capabilities [T1105].

entities.name: Ingress Tool Transfer

entities.name: Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI)
entities.evidence: Medusa actors use Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) [T1047] for querying system information.

entities.name: Use of Certutil
entities.evidence: Certutil (certutil.exe), an administrator utility used to manage public key infrastructure (PKI) and download files, is used to avoid detection when performing file ingress.

entities.name: Use of Minidump
entities.evidence: Medusa actors also use Minidump (comsvcs.dll) to avoid detection when dumping Local Security Authority Subsystem Service (LSASS) credentials.

entities.name: PowerShell Stealth Techniques
entities.evidence: Medusa actors use several different PowerShell stealth techniques with increasing complexity; these are provided below.

entities.name: PowerShell Base64 Encrypted Command
entities.evidence: In this example, Medusa actors use a well-known stealth technique that executes a base64 encrypted command [T1027.013] using specific execution settings.

entities.name: PowerShell Obfuscated DownloadFile
entities.evidence: In another example, the DownloadFile string is obfuscated by slicing it into pieces and referencing it via a variable [T1027].

entities.name: PowerShell Obfuscated Base64 Payload
entities.evidence: In the final example, the payload is an obfuscated base64 string read into memory, decompressed from gzip, and used to create a scriptblock.

entities.name: Deletion of PowerShell Command Line History
entities.evidence: Medusa actors attempt to cover their tracks by deleting the PowerShell command line history [T1070.003].
